# Data
The data set contains the variables `age` (age in years), `sex` (female = 0, male = 1), and `y` as a binary (e.g. disease) outcome.
```{r}
  data(logreg)
  data <- logreg
```


```{r}
summary(data[, c('sex', 'age', 'y')])
```
The mean for `y` is 0.1548, i.e. 15.5% of indidivual have disease status 1. Therefore, we cannot directly equate RR with OR, when interpreting results.

# Exercise 2: Sub-sample analyses

In this exercise, sub-samples of the data is analyzed.


## Analysis 2 (1:5 sampling)

First, identify the indeces of cases and controls in the data set with the `which` function. Determine the case/control ratio.

```{r}
Icases = which(data$y == 1);
Icontrols = which(data$y == 0)

length(Icontrols) / length(Icases)
```

Next, take a sample of 1000 cases and 5000 controls. Use the `sample` function to perform the sub-sampling.

```{r}
Ncases = 1000
Ncontrols = 5000
dataS = rbind(data[Icases[sample(Ncases)], ], data[Icontrols[sample(Ncontrols)], ])
```

Analyze the resulting data set as above, interpret.
